The South Asian Summer Monsoonal precipitation variability during the mid to late-Piacenzian (MPWP; 3.3 to 2.6 million years ago) was controlled by the Indonesian Throughflow and orbital parameters.
the SASM variability during the late Plicenzian was primarily controlled by the eccentricity of the earth's orbit, which is in line with the findings of previous studies.
the mid to late-Piacenzian SASM intensified (worsened) during the interglacial (glacial) periods of the late-Piacenzan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ITF in the SASM variability during the late Plicene.
the role of the tectonic reorganization of the ITF and the earth's orbital forcing in the long-term variability of the SASM.
the impact of the ITF on the SASM during a period of high atmospheric pCO 2 and provides a better understanding of the SASM response to the future climate changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mPWP was a period with enhanced SASM, which was modulated by the tectonic and orbital controls.
the SASM variability during the late Plicocene was primarily controlled by global climate forcing, but was influenced by the tectonics-induced changes in ITF.
the SASM was controlled by the earth's orbital forcing during the mPWP, and the ITF played a role in modulating the intensity of the SASM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SASM variability during the mPWP was controlled by the ITF reorganization and the earth's orbital forcing.
the SASM during late Pliocence was more sensitive to the earth's orbital forcing compared to the global climate, which was more sensitive to atmospheric pCO2.
during the late Pilocene, the SASM was more sensitive to the eccentricity than to the precessional cycle, and the ITF played a significant role in modulating the SASM intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SASM is sensitive to changes in pCO2 and ITF.
the SASM variability during the mPWP can be explained by the combined influence of global and local climate forcings.
the tectonic reorganization of ITF played a significant role in the long-term evolution of the SASM.
